pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK constraint and a default of normal. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test checks the exact list text for high, low and normal items.
The 'AC-3' test checks the high, low and normal filters and their id order.
The 'AC-4' test checks `/` lists all items in id order.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact nav markup for all four views.
The 'AC-6' test checks a 400 and no `<li>` for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.
The 'AC-7' test checks the exact messages for no match (high, low, normal) and for an empty table in all four views. The weakened 'No match' state test does not undo this.
traffic/routes.json contains `/?priority=high`, and the 'AC-8' test asserts it.

findings.what: Commit 543d455 ('Follow-up edits') loosened the 'No match' state test from `toBe("No low-priority items.")` to `toBeDefined()`. `message()` returns null when absent, and null is defined, so the assertion can never fail. The spec records no justification for this. The State-table row 'No match' therefore has no real message check in the states block. AC-7 covers the messages elsewhere.

The body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but commit 543d455 loosened an assertion in test/priority.test.js. The body also says 'Changed after the go: nothing', yet that follow-up commit came after the work.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening, or disclose it in the PR body with its reason.

findings.what: The README mentions the filter but not that other priority values answer 400, nor the high/low labels or the filter links.
findings.fix: Add a short note on the 400 response and the labels.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec. Beyond the spec it also relaxes the traffic route check to allow query strings, which AC-8 requires, and the PR discloses this.
All 8 acceptance items are met. Of the four State-table rows, 'No match' is only weakly tested in the states block (see finding). The spec was not edited.

The tests are generally behavioural and exact, but the 'No match' state assertion was loosened to an always-passing `toBeDefined()`. I did not run the tests: CI runs them, and the tests need the Cloudflare workers pool.
The README mentions the filter; the 400 behaviour and the labels are not documented (low finding).
The query is parameterised and the priority is validated against a whitelist. The nav and item output are escaped or built from constants. I found no defects.
The title is HTML-escaped and the priority value is whitelisted before use in SQL, the nav and the message. I found no planted instructions.
The change is a minimal server-rendered HTML list with no CSS or UI component files; this is not treated as a UI design review.
There is no browser session, and the diff touches no UI component files.
The PR body's 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim is false (see finding).
